They can verify the authenticity of validly signed certificates but fail to detect behavioral fraud throughout the certificate lifecycle. This paper presents SmartGate—a secure framework that combines AI and blockchain to detect behavioral fraud and protect the integrity of academic certificates. The framework uses AI and feature engineering to capture user behavioral patterns indicative of fraud. The proposed SmartGate is designed to screen a certificate’s behavioral context before allowing it to be stored on the blockchain. University student records data were used to evaluate the proposed SmartGate. Specifically, the normal academic records and certificate workflow are real, while the suspicious cases were synthetically generated via controlled fraud scenarios. A machine learning algorithm is used to model the relationship between user behavior and the legitimacy of certificates. The framework introduces an SHAP explainable AI approach to interpret the outcomes for transparency and trust. To provide a secure, tamper-proof system, blockchain is deployed to anchor the approved certificates. A prototype of the proposed SmartGate has been developed. As a proof-of-concept implementation, the XGBoost model was used to validate the certificate-screening stage of the proposed SmartGate system. Also, a local Ethereum environment was used to implement the blockchain anchoring stage. Experimental results demonstrate the technical feasibility of the proposed SmartGate framework, including its ability to provide feature-level model explainability, within a controlled environment.


This study presents a prototype of an integrated AI–blockchain framework for behavioral fraud detection within academic certificate processing and management. The SmartGate framework integrates pre-issuance AI behavioral screening with a blockchain certificate anchoring and verification. The studies in Table 2 were selected for their relevance to the design areas that most closely define our proposed framework. These areas include academic certificate verification, fraud detection, behavioral analysis, blockchain-based credential management, and explainable AI.

Image

Table 2. Comparison of related works.

## 3. Problem Statement

The use of technologies such as blockchain has enabled the storage of immutable certificates. Once a certificate is registered on a blockchain, it becomes tamper-proof. However, blockchain can accept and register any certificate hash that is validly signed. This means blockchain does not address the insider threat problem. For example, a registrar or administrator with legitimate access to the university system can be compromised and used to issue an illegal but validly signed certificate to a candidate. If the hash of this fraudulent but validly signed certificate is stored on the blockchain, the blockchain will provide immutability to the fraudulent certificate. In such a case, blockchain performs its function by providing security to the certificate even if it was fraudulent. What our SmartGate is built to do is to stop such suspicious certificates before they are wrongly registered on the blockchain. SmartGate analyses the behavioral context in which certificates are generated and issued to detect anomalies. If suspicious behaviors are detected, such certificates are dropped before blockchain anchoring. The proposed SmartGate thus provides an additional mechanism for supporting certificate integrity.
